output.headline: Sponsor with provider deal history and upper-quartile pricing; size and Midwest reach are the stretch, so a lower-priority call.
output.differentiator: Its median 15.7x paid sits above the comparable 75th percentile of 15.3x, so it can meet upper-quartile pricing. Peer lines were not available, so no lead over other buyers is claimed. [V:comps]
output.why_them: Provider-experienced sponsor that has paid upper-quartile multiples

acquirer_overview.title: A large sponsor with a steady, mostly control-oriented record
points: Financial sponsor with $303.0 billion in assets under management as of December 31, 2025 (TPG Inc.) [P:1].
18 deals between 2016 and 2023, of which 15 closed (83%); 17 of 18 were control deals [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share].
Ranks 9th on the priority list of 10, with a likelihood of 3.7% across 107 buyers scored [R:rank].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Provider experience supports fit, but the target would be a new bet
points: Prior purchases from similar sellers are a modest factor in its favour; deals in neighbouring sub-sectors are a slight one [S:own_fit_s, S:sector_rel].
Growth was a motive in 10 of 18 deals, against 41% across all deals in the file; the target grows 11.0% [M:high_growth, X:target].
It has 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 8 in adjacent provider sub-sectors, but no open platform to add onto [T:record, A:angles].

precedent_activity.title: Comparable-size provider deals exist, but few in the target's own space
points: Quality Medical Group: $187M minority investment in 2022, in the target's own sub-sector, at 11.2x EV/EBITDA [D:MA-2022-0350].
Granite Dental Network: $203M platform investment in 2021 at 12.2x; Liberty Addiction Treatment: $118M leveraged buyout in 2021 at 8.8x [D:MA-2021-0439, D:MA-2021-0369].
8 of 18 deals fall in the $100M-$400M size band, but the median deal is $88M [K:size_band, T:record].

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible, but returns at the ask fall short
points: 70 comparable deals show 10.7x, 12.8x and 15.3x EV/EBITDA at the 25th percentile, median and 75th percentile [V:comps].
Target margin of 16.8% against a comps median of 12.9% supports the 75th percentile; TPG's own median paid is 15.7x [V:comps].
At 5.0x leverage and a $128M equity cheque, IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target; maximum price is $216M with a 15.0x platform exit [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $88M is under half the $200M EV [C:conviction].
risk_flags.mitigant: 8 of 18 deals sit in the $100M-$400M band, and the biggest was $1,388M [K:size_band, T:record].
risk_flags.reality: It can write the cheque, but the target is well above its typical deal [T:record].

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target [V:lbo].
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M, against $193M at the same exit [V:lbo].
risk_flags.reality: The bid works only if it underwrites a platform exit [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest and sub-sector footprint
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 of 18 deals was in the target's region, and buying there is a slight factor against [T:record, S:geo_fit].
risk_flags.mitigant: Geographic expansion was a motive in 14 of 18 deals, though that tag is common across the file [M:geographic_expansion].
risk_flags.reality: It has 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector, a minority stake, and no open platform [D:MA-2022-0350, A:angles].

conviction.rationale: Provider deal history is a positive (1 own-sub-sector deal, 8 adjacent), and there is no open platform. The median deal of $88M is under half the $200M EV, which weighs against. [C:conviction, T:record]
